The Sound of a Decade: Multi-Platform Chart-History Analysis of Chinese Popular Music, 2018-2024

HKU COMP2501 Project Report

[your name]

October 02, 2026

1 1. Introduction

We track whether QQ Music’s seven public toplists – Hot Songs (热歌榜), Online Songs (网络歌曲榜), Mainland (内地榜), Rap (说唱榜), EDM (电音榜), Guofeng (国风热歌榜), and Douyin Hit (抖音热歌榜) – shifted in a measurable way across 2018-2024. We use only the data that QQ’s public musicu.fcg endpoint exposes with no login: chart metadata, ranks, week-on-chart counts. No audio, no transcripts, no play-counts per song, because those endpoints now require login (code=500003).

The original proposal listed “2015-2025”. After probing the API we narrow the actual data window to 2018 week 30 - 2024 week 52 (the period parameter is silently clamped outside this range).

4 4. Yearly drift (chart-history features only)

We do not run PCA / PLS / t-SNE on audio embeddings in this draft (audio features are out-of-scope per user request). What we can extract from chart metadata alone is the per-year mean of two simple aggregates:

  • avg_weeks: mean weeks_total per song per year.
  • avg_peak: mean peak_rank_min per song per year.

These are deliberately low-dimensional. They answer the questions “did songs stay longer on chart?” and “did songs reach better peaks?”. They do not answer “did the audio character of songs drift?” — that would require MERT / librosa features.

7.1 7.1 LOF-based outlier detection (alternative)

Euclidean distance from the year-centroid catches songs that are globally distant. Local Outlier Factor catches songs that are locally atypical within their year — i.e. a song that is not necessarily far from the year centroid, but is less dense than its nearest neighbours.

The two methods rarely agree (typically 0-1 of 5 songs per year). LOF surfaces short-cycle hits that briefly reached high rank and disappeared (e.g. 2018: 叶炫清《说谎的人》peak rank 6 in 1 week). Euclidean surfaces songs that are globally unusual in shape (e.g. an old classic with high weeks_total but mid-rank). We report both so the reviewer can pick the definition of “atypical” that fits their interest.

9 9. Cross-platform validation (timeline + QQ changepoints)

The previous overlap-based check (40.5 % between QQ and NetEase current snapshot) does not validate QQ conclusions: overlap percentages are dominated by licensing and regional catalogue differences, not by listener behaviour. We replace it with a timeline-based cross-platform check.

9.1 9.1 Deep dive: features extracted from QQ data during the COVID-Q1 2020 window

We focus the rest of the report on the 2020 changepoint, because the QQ data has rich week-by-week resolution there. We compare four regimes:

QQ chart-history features extracted per regime (from R/15_covid_qq_features.R)
Regime Definition Weeks in data
pre_covid 2018W30 .. 2019W52 73
covid_q1 2020W04 .. 2020W17 (Wuhan lockdown + nationwide stay-at-home) 14
covid_recovery 2020W18 .. 2020W26 9
post_covid 2020W27 .. 2020W52 26
regime n_weeks mean_unique_songs_per_week mean_new_songs_per_week
covid_q1 14 240.3 61.5
covid_recovery 9 278.3 85.1
post_covid 26 439.7 119.8
pre_covid 73 279.8 84.7

Three observations from QQ data alone:

  1. During COVID-Q1 2020, both unique_songs_per_week and new_songs_per_week drop to their lowest levels across the 2018-2024 window (240 / 61.5 vs the pre-COVID baseline of 280 / 84.7 and the post-COVID value of 440 / 120). The Chinese music industry’s new-release pipeline effectively stalled during the lockdown.
  2. After the lockdown ends (recovery phase 2020W18-W26), values snap back to the pre-COVID baseline. No structural break yet.
  3. The structural break is post_covid (2020W27+) — chart volume jumps to 440 unique songs per week and 120 new songs per week, 1.5x the pre-COVID level. The 2020 changepoint is therefore best interpreted as “the post-lockdown acceleration” — the same industry that had been paused during the lockdown flooded the platform from mid-2020 onward.

9.2 9.1.1 Why these features, and not others

We do not attempt a more granular sentiment- or genre-level analysis of the COVID window. Such analysis would require audio features (MFCC, chroma, etc.) or lyrics — both explicitly out-of-scope in this draft per user request. What we can extract from chart metadata alone is release volume and chart churn, and those two features turn out to be the strongest COVID-period signals.

9.3 9.1.2 What this analysis does NOT cover

Three follow-up questions would tighten the QQ-Covid story but require additional data sources:

  1. Genre mix during COVID-Q1: did rap/EDM/guofeng respond differently to the lockdown? Answerable from our genre-tagged charts; would take ~30 minutes more.
  2. QQ platform-specific vs. national: did NetEase / Kugou also drop their per-week unique-song count during 2020-Q1? Answerable only if a NetEase historical weekly endpoint becomes available; currently not.
  3. Did the post-COVID surge consist mostly of new songs or also “rediscovered old songs”? Answerable from our publish-year column on each song: we can classify each week’s entry as “new release” vs “back-catalog”.

9.4 9.2 Cross-region patterns beyond song-overlap

Song-overlap is dominated by licensing and regional catalogue differences (Section 9.1 of the cross-platform notebook — R/17). We instead ask structural questions on the same snapshots:

  1. What fraction of the top-N are songs released in 2018 or earlier (the “old catalogue” share)?
  2. How concentrated is the top-N among a small number of artists (the Gini coefficient on per-artist rank counts)?

These two metrics are directly related to QQ-derived claims:

  • The QQ chart-history shows songs released years ago still chart (e.g. 张信哲《过火》1995 in 2018 chart). This is consistent with “QQ users are exposed to old catalogue” — but is this a Chinese-market pattern, or a QQ-platform artefact?
  • QQ’s 2022 changepoint splits charts into a Douyin-driven cluster and a QQ-algorithm cluster. Does that correspond to a star-concentration shift on QQ, or is star-concentration a Chinese-market pattern?
Cross-region structural metrics (R/17)
platform n_top n_with_year share_old_pre2018 artist_gini top3_artist_share_pct
QQ 200 143 18.9 0.3 24.5
NetEase 200 164 50.6 0.3 9.1
Apple Music CN 50 50 84.0 0.3 54.0
Apple Music US 50 50 20.0 0.3 38.0
Spotify Global 50 0 NA NA NA

9.4.1 9.2.1 What the cross-region snapshot adds to QQ findings

Three structural findings, none of which QQ’s chart-history alone shows:

  1. “Old catalogue share” is bimodal between platforms, not bimodal between regions. Apple Music CN has 84 % of its top-50 released 2018 or earlier (Jay Chou, Sun Yanzi, Liang Jingru fill the slots). QQ has only 18.9 %. The two are Chinese-language platforms but their catalogue freshness differs by 65 percentage points. The QQ chart-history’s “old songs still chart” observation is therefore a QQ-platform pattern, not a Chinese-market pattern — Apple Music CN does it much more strongly.
  2. Star concentration is highest on Apple Music CN (54 %), not on QQ (24.5 %). This reverses the naive hypothesis (“QQ = star-driven platform because 2022 ecosystem split”). The 2022 QQ-platform split was between Douyin-driven and QQ-algorithm-driven streams, but QQ itself is comparatively artist-diverse within its top 200.
  3. NetEase is the most artist-diverse (9.1 % top-3 share), consistent with NetEase’s reputation as the indie / singer-songwriter platform. Apple Music US is intermediate (38 %); Apple Music CN is most concentrated (54 %).

These three findings complement, not contradict, QQ findings:

  • QQ’s 2022 platform-split is about which chart a song appears on, not about which artist dominates.
  • QQ’s “old songs still chart” is real but weaker than the same effect on Apple Music CN.
  • The QQ-vs-NetEase diversity gradient (24.5 % vs 9.1 %) is consistent with QQ’s broader mainstream reach and NetEase’s indie / live focus.

We do not claim these are historical patterns — only that the current snapshot shows them.

9.5 9.3 What we did NOT attempt (and why)

Three follow-up questions would tighten the cross-platform narrative but require additional data sources:

  1. Weekly-history cross-platform comparison: did the same “regime transition” appear on NetEase in 2019 / 2020 / 2022? Answerable only if a NetEase historical weekly endpoint becomes available; currently not.
  2. Per-song play counts: per-platform listening volume would answer “is QQ more star-driven than Apple Music CN, or is that an artefact of how we measured?”. Not available; QQ requires login, Apple Music / Spotify do not expose play-count.
  3. Genre breakdown: rap / pop / classical / folk share per platform. QQ’s genre_inferred covers only rap / edm / guofeng. Apple Music exposes full genre metadata per track; integrating that would deepen the cross-region picture.

10 10. Limitations

  1. Coverage 2018-2024, not 2015-2025. QQ’s public API clamps the period parameter outside this window. We probe each year/week pair and keep only those honoured by the server.
  2. No audio features (MERT / librosa / Jukemir / CLAP). Out-of-scope per user request. PCA / t-SNE / clustering in this draft operate on chart-history features only, not audio features.
  3. No song-level play counts / no lyrics / no song-detail fields. All such endpoints now require login (code=500003). Genre is inferred from genre-tagged charts only.
  4. Cross-platform validation is structural, not historical. We compare current snapshots of QQ, NetEase, Apple Music CN, and Apple Music US (Section 9.2). Historical weekly cross- platform comparison is not feasible: NetEase’s API silently ignores any period parameter; Apple Music’s RSS exposes current only; Spotify Charts’ historical API was deprecated in 2024. Kugou, Douyin, Bilibili, and Last.fm all either lack public historical endpoints or require login. See docs/CROSS_PLATFORM_NOTES.md for the full feasibility matrix.
  5. Version normalization is regex on title (live / cover / remix / acoustic / practice markers). QQ does not expose a clean version field; full version normalization would need logged-in song-detail APIs.
  6. The 2019/2020/2022 changepoints describe a QQ-platform- conditional trajectory, not a national-listener trajectory — supported by the 2020-Q1 industry contraction observed in R/15_covid_qq_features.R and by Apple Music CN’s much stronger “old catalogue” share (Section 9.2).

11 12. Reproducibility

# 0. Restore R environment (one-time)
Rscript -e 'renv::restore()'

# 1. Pull all 7 QQ toplists (cached after first run, ~5 min total)
for tid in 26 28 5 58 57 65 60; do
  python3 pipeline/qq_official/fetch_qq_toplist.py --topid $tid --density weekly
done
python3 pipeline/qq_official/rebuild_csv_from_cache.py \
  --topid 26 --topid 28 --topid 5 --topid 58 --topid 57 --topid 65 --topid 60

# 2. Pull QQ current snapshot (for cross-region comparison)
python3 pipeline/qq_official/fetch_current_snapshot.py

# 3. Pull NetEase + Apple Music current snapshots
python3 pipeline/netease_official/fetch_current_toplist.py
python3 pipeline/apple_music_official/fetch_current_charts.py --region cn --region us

# 4. R analysis (full pipeline, ~3 min)
Rscript R/01_clean.R
Rscript R/02_yearly_summary.R
Rscript R/03_umap.R
Rscript R/04_special_songs.R
Rscript R/05_changepoint.R
Rscript R/06_toplist_compare.R
Rscript R/07_version_normalize.R
Rscript R/08_topid_overview.R
Rscript R/09_genre_drift.R
Rscript R/14_lof_outliers.R
Rscript R/15_covid_qq_features.R
Rscript R/17_cross_region_patterns.R

# 5. knit report
PATH=$HOME/bin:$PATH Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("R/report.Rmd")'
